messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: gpu-driver-reset rate > 20/min on cluster rtg-prod-gpu-pool. Pattern: repeated Xid 13 / driver resets. Auto-metric link: https://metrics.redwood/alerts/2249803333

emma (oncall): I'm on it. Pulling telemetry + recent driver logs now.

emma (oncall): quick check — are errors confined to a single AZ or spread across nodes?

raj (infra): Looks like spike centered on rtg-gpu-12..rtg-gpu-14 (rack-3). Other racks low.

maria (runtime): Seeing container restarts for model-serving-v2 on those nodes. Logs show repeated cuda driver reset and OOM-ish traces. Example:
```
[2026-03-15T10:02:11Z] runtime ERROR: cuda: driver reset detected (Xid 13) while executing kernel
[2026-03-15T10:02:11Z] runtime INFO: evicting KV cache for session abc123
[2026-03-15T10:02:12Z] container ERROR: oom-kill event? process killed by SIGKILL
```

noah (support): Got a couple of customer reports referencing "500 internal error" and timeouts around 10:02-10:15 UTC. Collecting request ids.

chris (customer-success): I'll draft a holding note for affected tenants. Need a list of endpoints impacted and rough user count. ping me when you have the mapping.

emma (oncall): Root cause hypothesis: intermittent ECC/thermal -> driver resets -> container crashes -> pod churn. Plan: cordon + drain noisy nodes, migrate pods, throttle autoscaler for pool, and hardware ticket if persists. Assigning tasks: raj infra + maria runtime + chris comms.

raj (infra): Agreed. Recommendation: set node pool autoscale min to current to avoid rapid reschedules, then cordon. Also prefer graceful drain to avoid double-scheduling to same pool.

emma (oncall): Executing cordon/drain for rtg-gpu-12 then rtg-gpu-13. Commands:
```bash
kubectl cordon rtg-gpu-12
kubectl drain rtg-gpu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120
```
I'll run one at a time.

incident-bot: Status update: mitigation in progress — nodes rtg-gpu-12..13 cordoned, silence set for alert group gpu-driver-reset-pool for 30m.

maria (runtime): NVML shows ECC correctable error rate spike on rtg-gpu-13. dmesg excerpt: 
```
[  123.456789] NVRM: Xid (31): Ch 00000001, pid 8245, GPU 00000000:01:00.0
[  123.457001] NVRM: Xid (13): 0xb0000000E 
[  123.458000] nv_peer_mem: vendor 10de device 1db6 
```
Also seeing thermal margins rising on the same GPU. Suspect hardware/intermittent ECC faults.

chris (customer-success): Customer impact summary: three tenants reported errors — two high-traffic (prod) and one staging. Estimated ~120k requests in the window, ~0.8% error rate increase for the prod tenants. Draft ready for review.

noah (support): Pulling request_id list + endpoints. DMing chris the CSV now.

raj (infra): Rebooted rtg-gpu-12 after drain. Driver reloaded cleanly, no immediate Xid. Watching. For rtg-gpu-13 I recommend hardware swap if Xid recurrence > 3 in 30m. I'll open a hardware ticket with datacenter ops.

emma (oncall): For failover we switched routing for heavy-tenants to variant model v2-lite (fp16/quantized) in eu-west to preserve throughput. Routing policy updated: prefer eu-west fallback for model-serving-v2 endpoints.

maria (runtime): Added temporary kernel boot param to log NVML earlier and increase nv_driver debug level. Also toggled prefix cache so noisy sessions don't evict others.

emma (oncall): Oncall handoff in ~45m. Leaving runbook notes: 
- nodes: rtg-gpu-12 drained & rebooted (monitoring), rtg-gpu-13 cordoned, hardware ticket #HW-22498 open.
- actions taken: cordon/drain, routing fallback to v2-lite, autoscale min locked, CS notified.
- observability: perf graph link: https://metrics.redwood/graph/gpu-driver-resets/2249803333

olga (eng-releases): Acknowledged handoff. I'll take watch and escalate if Xid > 2 in next 30m. Please ping on call if anything changes.

incident-bot: Update: monitoring phase. If driver resets reoccur, incident will escalate to hardware oncall automatically.

emma (oncall): Leaving now for scheduled break; olga is ondeck. If anyone sees new Xids or container churn, ping @olga + @raj.

olga (eng-releases): Watching dashboards. Thanks team.

incident-bot: Thread timestamp: 2249803333 | last update: 2249804745 | state: monitoring
